chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman al-Azramy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if a man eats while he is walking; the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do that.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ: He used to do that (indicating established practice)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat while walking in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility (juz') of eating while walking, citing the practice of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and Imam Ali (peace be upon him) as precedents. It falls under the category of social etiquette and minor jurisprudential rulings regarding daily actions. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often contextualized within the broader principle of *ibahah* (original permissibility) unless specific evidence indicates otherwise, highlighting the flexibility of Sunnah in daily conduct.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman Al Azramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if the man eat and he is walking, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had done that’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from the one who narrated to him from ‘ Abd al- Rahman al-‘Arzamiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘It is not unlawful if a man eats while walking. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, ate while walking.’”
